rationale: bugs_open/160: verify_report_prose is the deterministic gate between the LLM prose steps and the report page, and it is deliberately fail-closed -- a violation means no page is composed at all. Its SKU classifier rejects a token unless that token appears VERBATIM in the fact block / request context or overlaps a scored candidate name. But the writer legitimately RECOMBINES an allowed token into an English phrase, and a recombination is never verbatim. Measured live 2026-07-31: of the 2 retained report orchestrations, 1 died on `summary_html names model-like token "IP54-or-better" not in the candidate set or fact block` (work item 4ccc73d7-c467-480f-9a39-0b327b383870, 08:20Z, chassis v1.0.1213) -- IP54 IS in the fact block, put there by buildFactBlock's 'required protection IP54' line; only the composed phrase is new. The report was destroyed and https://robot-hands.com/reports/bf3765d6-....html returned 404. The class is wider than the instance and is confirmed by unit test, not inferred: IP54-rated, M6-compatible (the substring modelNumberRe actually extracts from a paraphrase of the ISO flange code ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6) and 2F-85-compatible are all rejected today by the same rule. It is intermittent, because the trigger is generated wording -- the identical spec passed this gate on 2026-07-27 -- so it presents as a flaky pipeline rather than as a rule, and a retry 'fixes' it. Blast radius measured, not assumed: exactly ONE active agent definition contains this action (report-builder; 1 row, is_active, non-snapshot), so no other pipeline's guarantee changes. Intent: keep the guard strict on the thing it exists to stop -- a sibling model number invented by the writer -- while ceasing to destroy reports over English suffixes. The fail-closed behaviour is NOT touched: 016b and the prior council HIGH of 2026-07-28 (corr 721ac4f7) both establish it is right, and downgrading the violation to a warning would reopen the fabrication class the reports pipeline exists to prevent.

plan.summary: The SKU check gains a third and narrowest route to clearance: a token also traces when it splits into a HEAD that traces by the existing two routes and a TAIL whose every hyphen segment is an ordinary English qualifier word. modelNumberRe puts the letter-digit adjacency in the first segment, so the code-bearing part is always inside the head -- this relaxes which SUFFIXES are tolerated, never whether the model number itself was published. The two routes that exist today are unchanged and tried first, so nothing cleared today changes; this is purely additive relaxation of check (2). The numeric gate, the vendor gate, the no-match contract, the truncation guard and the fail-closed contract are all untouched.

edits.rationale: Extracts the existing inline clearance test unchanged (verbatim in allowedText, then candidate-name overlap) and adds route 3, the head/tail decomposition. Any split point is accepted, which is equivalent to taking the longest traceable head: a shorter head only moves MORE segments into the tail, and a code segment in the tail fails the qualifier test anyway. The security property is that the head must still trace by route 1 or 2, and modelNumberRe guarantees segment 0 carries the letter-digit adjacency -- so 2F-140 is still rejected (head '2F' traces, tail '140' carries a digit) while IP54-or-better clears (head 'IP54' traces, tail 'or'/'better' are English).

The whole risk of this change lives here, so every clause is justified by the fabrication it rejects and each is mutation-checked against its own counterexample: no digit rejects 2F-140 and GEP5010IO-00-B (a digit in the tail IS a variant number); at least 2 characters rejects 2F-85-x; all lower-case rejects 2F-85-XL (upper-case codes are SKU suffix material, English qualifiers are not). The bug file's own suggestion -- clear a segment when it is 'digit-free English' -- was NOT taken, because digit-free alone clears an invented sibling's single-letter and upper-case suffixes, which is precisely what the guard exists to stop. Two residuals are stated in the code rather than absorbed: a title-cased qualifier (IP54-Rated) is not cleared, and a lower-case invented suffix (2F-85-plus) is. Both would be answered by a closed vocabulary of qualifier words; it is not built because no instance of either has been observed, and the asymmetry favours strictness -- an over-strict rejection produces a retry whose different phrasing usually passes (016b records this very report doing so), while an under-strict clearance publishes a fabricated model number in a customer-facing report.

Call site only: the inline clearance test becomes a call to skuTokenTraces. The violation message is deliberately unchanged so existing tests, the 016b entry and the recorded live error text all still match.

Both halves, because 016b's entry for this pattern says in terms that a fix asserted only on the first half is how a strictness guard gets quietly disarmed. The accept test asserts the SPECIFIC violation ('model-like token') is absent as well as len(v)==0, because the numeric gate would otherwise absorb a mutation of the SKU rule and the test would keep passing for the wrong reason -- the landmine recorded 2026-07-31. The reject test names the token AND the check in its assertion for the same reason. Both run against realScoring over the live-mirror fixture index, so they bind against what production actually produces. Mutation-checked, one clause at a time: dropping route 3 fails the accept test on IP54-or-better; dropping the case clause lets 2F-85-XL through; dropping the length clause lets 2F-85-x through. The first run of that check found MY OWN test case was wrong -- the length clause was pinned with an upper-case 2F-85-X, which the case clause already rejects, so the clause was untested until the case was lower-cased.

grounded_in: live __step_error, 1 of 2 retained report orchestrations: 'step verify_prose failed: failed to execute action verify_report_prose: report prose failed verification (1 violations): summary_html names model-like token "IP54-or-better" not in the candidate set or fact block'

verify_report_prose_action.go:241 modelNumberRe = `\b[A-Za-z0-9]*(?:[A-Za-z][0-9]|[0-9][A-Za-z])[A-Za-z0-9]*-[A-Za-z0-9-]+\b` -- the adjacency is in the pre-hyphen segment, which is why the head always carries the code part, and why a paraphrase of ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 is extracted as the sub-token 'M6-compatible'
verify_report_prose_action.go:317 clearance was `if strings.Contains(allowedText, tok) { continue }` -- verbatim containment, which a recombination can never satisfy
score_grippers_action.go:737-739 buildFactBlock writes 'required protection IP%d' when req.IPMin > 0 -- this is how IP54 is in the fact block while IP54-or-better is not
blast radius query: SELECT type, is_active FROM agent_definitions WHERE default_config::text LIKE '%verify_report_prose%' AND deleted_at IS NULL -> exactly 1 row, report-builder, active, non-snapshot

016b section 9 (2026-07-31): 'verify a fix on BOTH halves: the legitimate recombination must clear AND a fabricated sibling must still be rejected. A fix asserted only on the first half is how a strictness guard gets quietly disarmed -- and the prefix-matching fix that suggests itself first clears exactly the invented-sibling SKU the guard exists to catch.'
